results.blind_working: The modern periodic law (Moseley) says properties are periodic functions of atomic number.
1-1-5 gives un-un-pent plus the suffix -ium, so the name is Ununpentium.
Period 4 fills 4s (1 orbital), 3d (5) and 4p (3). That is 9 orbitals holding 18 electrons.
A is true: the lanthanoids are placed separately at the bottom. R is false: lanthanoids belong to period 6 and fill the 4f orbitals; 5f describes the actinoids.
Statement I is incorrect: period 3 fills only 3s and 3p, not 3d. Statement II is incorrect: Moseley found that the square root of the frequency is proportional to Z, not the frequency itself.
The block is set by the subshell (s, p, d or f) that receives the last, differentiating electron.
[Ar]3d5 4s1 is Cr. For a d-block element, group = (n-1)d + ns electrons = 5 + 1 = 6.
This is Te. Highest shell n = 5 gives period 5. The last electron enters 5p, so it is p-block. Group = 10 + 2 + 4 = 16.

s-block: reactive metals with low ionization enthalpy (A-II). p-block: contains metals, non-metals and metalloids (B-IV). d-block: variable oxidation states, coloured ions, paramagnetism (C-III). f-block: inner transition elements including transuranium elements (D-I).
A, B and C are true. D is false because metallic character decreases across a period. E is false because the representative elements are the s- and p-block, not s- and d-block.

A non-metal does not have a metallic radius. Its cation would be smaller than the neutral atom. The van der Waals radius is half the distance between non-bonded atoms, so it exceeds the covalent radius and is the largest.

All four species have 10 electrons. Nuclear charge rises in the order N(7) < F(9) < Na(11) < Al(13). A higher nuclear charge pulls the same electrons closer, so radius decreases in that order: N3- > F- > Na+ > Al3+.
The covalent radius is half the bond length: 198/2 = 99 pm.
Ga (about 135 pm) is smaller than Al (about 143 pm), so A is true. This happens because 3d electrons shield the nucleus poorly, not effectively, so R is false.

Noble gas radii are van der Waals radii, which are large, so they are not the smallest in their periods; I is false. Zr and Hf have nearly equal radii because of the lanthanoid contraction; II is true.
Helium has the highest first ionization enthalpy, about 2372 kJ/mol. Its 1s² electrons are very close to the nucleus and have no shielding.
Approximate first ionization enthalpies: B 801, Be 899, C 1086, O 1314, N 1402 kJ/mol. So B < Be < C < O < N.
The big jump comes between the 2nd (1451) and 3rd (7733) ionization enthalpies. So X has two valence electrons; the values match Mg, a Group 2 element.

A: Be > B because an s electron penetrates more than a p electron (II). B: N > O because of paired-electron repulsion in O's 2p orbital (I). C: Na's second ionization breaks a noble gas core (IV). D: ionization enthalpy falls down a group due to larger size and more shielding (III).

A is true: ionization is endothermic. B is false: the second ionization enthalpy is always larger than the first. C is true: S (1000) < P (1012) kJ/mol. D is false: Al (577) < Mg (738) kJ/mol. E is true: Cs has the lowest among stable elements. So A, C and E.
Cl has the most negative electron gain enthalpy, about -349 kJ/mol. F is only about -328 kJ/mol because of electron repulsion in its compact 2p subshell.
The approximate values are O -141, S -200, Se -195 and Te -190 kJ/mol. O is anomalously low because of its small size, so the order of magnitude is S > Se > Te > O.
Ne has a noble gas configuration and Be has a filled 2s subshell, so both are positive. N has a stable half-filled 2p subshell, so its value is nearly zero or positive.
A is true because adding an electron to O- is opposed by electrostatic repulsion. R is a correct general periodic trend but does not explain A.
Statement I is false because F is less negative than Cl. Statement II is false because the values are swapped: O is about -141 and S is about -200 kJ/mol.
F is always -1, so x + 2(-1) = 0 and x = +2.
Group 15, period 3 is phosphorus. Its hydride is PH3, and in the highest oxide P4O10 the oxidation state is +5.
The inert pair effect stabilises the state two below the group oxidation state: Tl +1, Pb +2, Bi +3.
Cl in Cl2O7 is +7; O in OF2 is +2; O in Na2O is -2; S in SO3 is +6. So A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

A is true: B has no d orbitals, so its maximum covalency is 4. B is true: [AlF6]3- exists. C is false: Be's diagonal relationship is with Al. D is true: H2O, H2S. E is false: F, the most electronegative element, is always -1. Correct set is A, B, D.
Fluorine has the highest Pauling electronegativity (3.98), above O (3.44), Cl (3.16) and N (3.04).
BeO, ZnO and SnO are all amphoteric. Na2O is basic, SO3 and SiO2 are acidic, so options 1, 2 and 4 each contain a non-amphoteric oxide.
Li has the highest ionization enthalpy in group 1. Its very small ion has a very large hydration enthalpy, which outweighs this and gives the most negative E°.
Cl2O7 is the anhydride of HClO4, a very strong acid, so its aqueous solution is strongly acidic. R is true and directly explains A.
Statement I is false: Al2O3 is amphoteric and reacts with both HCl and NaOH. Statement II matches NCERT: reactivity is lowest in the centre of a period, and halogens are strong oxidisers.
